rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Design and measurement - HOBO-U30 soil moisture probes (0-200 cm, 2-h interval, May-Aug 2017) in one flood and one mulched-drip section at South Tallin Aile Village, plus monthly groundwater depth from seven monitoring wells 2014-2018. Q2: Results, Changes in groundwater depth and Figure 5 - flood irrigation shows stronger and quicker groundwater response to rainfall infiltration than mulched drip; flood area at ~8 m rises 0.98 m one month after >300 mm monthly rainfall, drip area at 4-5 m rises 0.77 m only after three months and shows no response at 6 m; Conclusions restate flood has stronger rainfall-infiltration replenishment than mulched drip. Q3: two independent observations - soil moisture profile monitoring (Figure 4: each rainfall raises soil moisture at 50 and 100 cm under flood, none under drip for small rains) and groundwater well level dynamics (Figure 5). Q4: Results, Changes in soil moisture content and Figure 4 - infiltration through the soil profile (intermediate variable for recharge) measured at 50, 100, 160, 200 cm; after 72 mm storm moisture at 2 m rose 1.4% at 14 d under flood vs 0.9% at 19 d under drip. Q6: Changes in groundwater depth - seven monitoring wells across Horqin Left Wing Middle Banner (four in mulched-drip area, three in flood area), i.e. district-level groundwater response. Q7: Results - authors state recharge response occurs only when rainfall is heavy (soil moisture at 100 cm rises only when rainfall reaches 72 mm; groundwater rises only when monthly rainfall exceeds 300 mm) and only at shallow groundwater depth (no response at ~8 m flood / 6 m drip); small-rain infiltration under flood stays within 1.6 m and is lost to evaporation. Q8: Changes in groundwater depth - due to limited research conditions only soil moisture to 2 m was monitored while groundwater depth exceeded 3 m, so soil data cannot directly show recharge.
rows.notes: The drip system studied is drip under plastic film mulch; the authors attribute much of the lower rainfall infiltration to the impermeable mulch intercepting rain, and the absence of irrigation return water under drip is asserted in the mechanism analysis rather than measured. The passage's causal attribution to return flows is therefore not directly tested, though the effect (flood > drip recharge) is observed. Single site/season for soil moisture (one soil profile, 2017); groundwater wells differ in depth between areas, which confounds the comparison. No standard deviations, ranges or confidence intervals reported.

notes: Full text available; figures referenced but not reproduced. Study is a short observational comparison of flood vs mulched drip irrigation in West Liaohe Plain, China, combining soil moisture probe data and groundwater well records.
